full_judgment:
2. The petitioners have filed the said title suit for declaration of their title in respect of .05 acre of land of Mouja Bagura Alekanda in the town of Barisal. While describing the suit land in the schedule of the plaint the plaintiffs described the suit plot as RS plot No. 7072. The defendant opposite parties filed written statement alleging, inter alia, that the identity of the suit land was in confusion because no corresponding CS plot was given in the schedule of the plaint. In this context the plaintiffs obtained an order for local investigation for relayment of the suit land of RS Plot No. 7072 and to find out its corresponding CS plot. The Advocate Commissioner was directed to relay the suit land of RS plot No. 7072 and find out from which CS plot this RS plot has arisen and to submit his report. The Advocate Commissioner complied with the writ and submitted his report dated 2.1.92 wherein the learned Advocate Commissioner, has very clearly stated that the corresponding CS plot of the suit plot being RS plot No. 7072 case 5073/4315  and not plot No. 5073. The said CS plot arose from CS plot No. 4315. Commissioner's report was accompanied by a sketch map and field book. He has stated in his report, inasmuch as, shown in the sketch map and the field book that .05 decimal of land which claimed to be the suit land as has been recorded in the said RS plot No. 7072 comprises actually .04 decimal of land and remaining .01 decimal of the suit land is part of the previous Zila Board Road which runs touching the northern side of the suit land. Learned Advocate Commissioner while prepared the sketch map and the field book considered carefully the position of the CS Khatian and some boundary pillars stations and by relayment of the disputed land observing all formalities submitted his report. The defendants-opposite parties filed a written objection alleging that the report should not be accepted as the Advocate Commissioner has not submitted his report in accordance with the writ delivered to him and that some statements have been made in the report by the Advocate Commissioner which are not relevant for the purpose of disposal of the suit and thus the defendants have been prejudiced. 

 4. Mr. Abdul Quayum, the learned Advocate for the petitioners representing the plaintiffs’ petitioners, took me to the report of the Advocate Commissioner. I have carefully gone through the same and I find that the learned Advocate Commissioner in his report distinctly mentioned that the corresponding CS plot No.  5073/4315 of RS plot No. 7072 and the said CS plot arose from original CS plot No.4315 and the area of the said plot also has been stated being 0.04 acre and he has also stated that the RS record was prepared in respect of .05 decimal of land including 0.01 decimal of land from the Zilla Board Road which runs touching northern side of the suit land. I find that the learned Advocate Commissioner has submitted his report after proper relayment of the suit land. In doing so he carefully examined the CS khatian and the position of some permanent stations pillars. Thus the Advocate Commissioner has not committed any illegality in submitting his report.
